name: desktop-hypervisor-mcp
description: VirtualBox and VMware Fusion/Workstation behind one provider-neutral MCP tool surface.
long_description: One MCP server for the desktop hypervisors: VirtualBox, VMware Fusion, and VMware Workstation. Nine capability-based tools cover VM lifecycle, snapshots, guest execution, networking, and verified downloads of official OS images. Providers advertise what they can actually do, so unsupported operations fail by naming the missing capability rather than with a raw provider error. With one hypervisor installed it is selected automatically; with several, the ambiguity is surfaced, never guessed.

tools.name: provider
tools.description: Installed hypervisors with status, capabilities, formats, and remediation

tools.name: artifact
tools.description: Verified downloads of official OS images, resolved per provider

tools.name: vm_lifecycle
tools.description: Create, start, stop, suspend, reset, delete, clone, import, export VMs

tools.name: vm_info
tools.description: List and inspect VMs, and discover guest IP addresses

tools.name: vm_config
tools.description: Resources, nested virtualization, ISO attachment, pre-boot guestinfo injection

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: Take, restore, delete, and list VM snapshots

tools.name: guest
tools.description: Execute commands and scripts in a guest, copy files, capture screenshots

tools.name: network
tools.description: Cluster networks, guest port exposure, and ISO mastering

tools.name: execute_command
tools.description: Raw VBoxManage / vmrun argv on the selected provider

guest_user.title: Guest username
guest_user.description: Username for in-guest operations (guest exec, script, file copy). Leave empty if you do not need guest operations.

guest_password.title: Guest password
guest_password.description: Password for in-guest operations. Stored securely by the host application and passed to the server as an environment variable, never as a tool parameter.

image_dir.title: Image cache directory
image_dir.description: Where downloaded OS images are cached. Defaults to ~/.hypervisor-images when empty.
